records.specification_basis: Porsche places the 10.3-inch color display in the center of the dashboard, and the full-resolution cockpit photograph shows the display behind the wheel rather than in the wheel's control face. Porsche's launch material explicitly describes the upper-open rim. Because the rim is a fixed-grip gt-formula/motorsport wheel rather than a continuous round or D-shaped band, the schema records open-top construction as not-applicable, matching the existing record. The full-resolution image shows fixed molded grips at left and right around a central control face, not a continuous band. Porsche identifies the wheel as a CFRP motorsport wheel with paddles and controls; this is the project's gt-formula category. The full-resolution cockpit photograph shows no distinct shift-light strip mounted on the wheel. Porsche's specification mentions illuminated push buttons, which are not the same as wheel-mounted shift lights; the display and its indicators are separate dashboard equipment. PMR and Porsche Motorsport identify a six-speed sequential transmission; the Porsche technical manual specifies six forward gears and ratios 1 through 6. Porsche calls the transmission sequential dog-type, the technical specification repeats dog-type construction, and the manual describes the 992 unit as a sequential claw/dog gearbox. Porsche's launch material states that gear changes are made by steering-wheel paddles; the technical specification identifies paddle shift with an electronic shift-barrel actuator, and the manual lists the right paddle for upshift and left paddle for downshift. The manufacturer calls the gearbox sequential and the manual gives a 1-to-6 / 6-to-1 sequential paddle path; no H-pattern gate is involved. The manual documents a dry racing clutch and clutch pedal, and its neutral-to-first engagement condition requires clutch pressure. That establishes a driver-operated clutch input for selecting first gear and moving away; the PMR staged no-clutch start is not promoted. The manual's 1-to-6 upshift table specifies the right paddle and shows no clutch-pressure requirement. The upshift table gives a throttle condition above 30 percent and does not require a lift; the documented running upshift is therefore no-lift. The documented upshift path is a paddle/no-clutch/no-lift action; the manual does not describe a manual throttle blip for upshift. Manual blip is not the applicable control for this upshift path. The manual documents automatic blip on the downshift path, not on upshift. No automatic upshift blip is part of the documented upshift procedure. The 6-to-1 downshift table lists the left paddle, automatic blip, and no clutch-pressure requirement. The downshift table defines the accelerator condition below 3 percent together with automatic blip rather than a separate driver lift instruction. Under the project's sequential/automatic-blip convention this field is not-applicable, not a claim that throttle position never changes during braking. The manual's downshift condition specifies paddle selection, accelerator below 3 percent, and automatic blip; it does not describe an automatic cut on downshift. Under the project's documented downshift model, cut is not-applicable. The manual explicitly assigns the throttle event to 'Auto. Blip' on the 6-to-1 downshift path, so the driver does not supply a manual rev-matching blip. The exact 992 Cup technical manual explicitly labels the 6-to-1 downshift throttle event 'Auto. Blip', establishing automatic rev matching. The reviewed sources did not establish the remaining technique and wheel fields, which stay unknown in the real-car baseline: /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/automatic_cut.
